summary: Created “Fleet Internal CA” on node1, issued a node2 certificate with DNS and IP SANs, trusted the CA system-wide on both nodes, and configured persistent HTTPS on node2:8443. Both nodes were restarted sequentially and fully recovered with changed boot identities.
actions_performed: Generated and retained the CA on node1.
Issued node2’s TLS certificate for DNS node2 and IP 10.100.71.11.
Installed the CA into both RHEL system trust stores.
Configured an enabled systemd HTTPS service and persistent firewalld rule for TCP/8443 on node2.
Verified trusted HTTPS locally and remotely with hostname validation.
Restarted node1 and node2 individually and verified persistence and recovery.

evidence.requirement: Create Fleet Internal CA and issue node2 TLS certificate
evidence.summary: Shows the CA identity, signed node2 certificate, DNS/IP SANs, successful chain validation, and hostname verification.

evidence.requirement: Serve trusted HTTPS on node2 port 8443
evidence.summary: Shows the enabled active service, 0.0.0.0:8443 listener, successful HTTPS response, and trusted remote validation before and after restarts.

evidence.requirement: Install CA as a trusted system authority on node1 and node2
evidence.summary: Shows Fleet Internal CA as a system trust anchor and successful system-path certificate verification on both nodes, including after restart.
Healthy baseline boot ID 03273aa8-4706-4e1c-a855-c6ae9635951d, safe reboot acknowledgement, changed boot ID df0d1cc4-f0e4-4d0d-a9c4-b2b8bc78178c, and recovered CA/trust/HTTPS state.

Healthy baseline boot ID b953e8ce-b303-4022-826c-3b5910ad1e9b, safe reboot acknowledgement, changed boot ID 904c7623-53af-42ec-92e8-791698ee3592, recovered service/listener/firewall/trust data, and independent HTTPS validation from node1.
